title: Pilot real TD sentries on the first map in an isolated practice mode
context: The owner wants Sniper to feel like taking control of a sentry inside the actual Stalheart TD game, using its first map rather than a separate range stage.
outcome: A Workshop link opens index.html?sentryPilot=1#td. The ordinary seed-7/500-point first-sector world, wall cells, Stalheart, breaches, waves and combat simulation remain game-owned. Six supplied wall mounts accept the eight numbered Sentries; Q/E transfers between posts, 1–8 changes the selected weapon, mouse/Space gates actual tower fire, wheel zooms and M switches optic/map. The game-side adapter owns input, optic and HUD; existing tower mechanics own traverse, range, damage, projectiles, effects and audio. The radar follows the mount. The tank stays parked and automatic fire is disabled; inactive mounts stay silent. Practice storage is document-memory-only. Heptapod is explicitly tethered to a missile emplacement without autonomous walking/cassette AI. This is an experiment, not a progression or balance promotion. Real-enemy tests also exposed absent spawn IDs; normal and fixture spawn paths now allocate stable document-lifetime IDs so missile locks and arrival damage identify the intended creature.
alternatives: Retain the existing Sniper bench and add an opt-in game mode instead of copying the TD map and simulation into a lab controller.
The first site-selection draft mapped a typed tag array to cell indices and truncated the indices; Array.from now preserves actual grid cell identities.

Initial optic/HUD capture showed tank controls overlapping the new HUD and a view above the breach. The mode now uses a mount-facing optic, compact controls, and wall positions farther back from the opening.
